verdict.rationale: Riveter documents AI agents that interpret pages the way a person would, with no selectors, and enrichments that fill columns via AI and web scrapes. However, the user typically names the fields to extract (Attributes: "CEO", "Employee Count"). Evidence that the LLM itself decides which structured fields to pull is limited to building from a natural-language prompt. missing for 10: documented LLM-driven schema/field inference from a page, explicit single-page structured-extraction docs (scrape only returns parseable text), independent or hands-on corroboration of extraction quality.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an LLM read a page and decide what structured fields to pull out without pre-written selectors

citations.quote: Riveter uses AI agents that interpret pages the way a person would, so the same configuration keeps working after a redesign.
An enrichment takes rows of input data and fills in new columns using AI, web searches, web scrapes, and other tools.
You can build one from a natural-language prompt or a structured spec, and Riveter will generate the rows for you.
extract data from complicated websites programmatically
